thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming.tail_p99 > 3x SLO for last 5m (region: us-west). Affected route: /v1/live/stream. Paging oncall.
maya (oncall): ack, seeing the page. I'm on it. Can someone grab proxy logs + recent deploys? :mag:
sam (eng-runtime): looking at runtime metrics now. No deploys in last 12h. p95 bumped to ~650ms, p99 -> 3200ms for chunk latencies.
ravi (eng-sre): pushing an initial hypothesis: keepalive churn + slow consumers causing proxy write buffers to pile up. Seen similar spike earlier but not this magnitude.
jules (support): getting customer reports: 3 customers reporting long stalls / stalled SSE streams — one customer says client receives heartbeat then silence for ~30s.
anita (eng-platform): forwarding SLO dashboard: https://redwood-monitoring.internal/d/streams/streaming-slo?orgId=1&var-region=us-west
maya (oncall): run `kubectl logs` for proxy pod group? Also check alb timeouts.
kevin (network): ALB 504s are flat. No mass 502s. But I see increased long-lived connections count on the proxy nodes.
sam (eng-runtime): grabbing proxy logs -> piping out recent writes that timed out:

```
2026-03-15T02:45:12Z proxy-7fdc WRITE_TIMEOUT conn=10.34.21.6 route=/v1/live/stream client_id=acct-42
2026-03-15T02:45:13Z proxy-7fdc BUFFER_FULL conn=10.34.23.11 inflight=120
2026-03-15T02:45:14Z proxy-7fdc DROP_CONN conn=10.34.23.11 reason=slow_consumer
```

maya (oncall): those BUFFER_FULL lines match the p99 spike windows. Any recent config changes to proxy keepalive or buffer sizes?
anita (eng-platform): no config pushes in last 24h. We did roll out a different batching tweak in runtime 3 days ago but it shouldn't affect proxies directly.
ravi (eng-sre): quick mitigation options: 1) enable aggressive slow-consumer throttling (drop after X missed heartbeats), 2) reduce proxy write buffer max_inflight, 3) temporary route-heavy customers to eu-west fallback region.
maya (oncall): customers impacted include high-throughput live chat and one voice-note transcription stream. Need live mitigation that avoids global outage.
jules (support): customer-rep-bot posted a ticket update template — want me to notify them we're investigating and may route traffic? :phone:
maya (oncall): yes please. Use: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls impacting a subset of live connections in us-west. We're applying mitigations now and will update in 15m."
kevin (network): I can flip a config on the proxy fleet to lower `max_write_inflight` from 256 -> 96 and enable `fast_drop_slow_consumers=true` for the us-west ASG. That should reduce buffer build-up but may increase disconnects for very slow clients.
sam (eng-runtime): risk: disconnects will cause some clients to reconnect and possibly spike auth checks. We can also enable non-streaming fallback for a small percentage to reduce continuous streaming pressure: route 10% of new stream sessions to short-poll endpoint with chunking disabled.
maya (oncall): proceed with both mitigations as a canary: kevin do the proxy change on one AZ first, sam do fallback routing for new sessions. Ravi monitor for auth spike.
kevin (network): starting AZ-a now. command: `infractl proxy set --asg us-west-a --max_write_inflight 96 --fast_drop true` — applying.

```
infractl: rolling update started (us-west-a)
infractl: 10/10 proxies updated
```

kevin (network): AZ-a updated. Observability shows in-flight per-pod drop ~40% and buffer events reduced.
ravi (eng-sre): tracing p99, still high but trending down. Heartbeat miss alarms decreased from 67 -> 18 in the last 3m.
sam (eng-runtime): enabling fallback routing rule: 10% sample keyed by customer_id hashed -> fallback endpoint `/v1/live/fallback-poll`.

```
runtimectl: route rule applied (us-west) sample=10%
```

maya (oncall): any impact to RBAC or auth during reconnects?
sam (eng-runtime): auth QPS up ~12% but within provisioned. No errors yet. Reconnection churn normal.
jules (support): updated customers: first customer reports partial recovery, second still seeing 15-20s stalls.
maya (oncall): keep monitoring for 10m. If p99 remains > 2xSLO, we escalate to full cross-region failover.
anita (eng-platform): I'm preparing a hotfix to proxy config that also reduces write buffer retention time (ttl) for idle streams. Can push if needed.
kevin (network): AZ-b queued for change, will roll after we validate AZ-a metrics for another 5m.

[5 minutes later]

ravi (eng-sre): p99 down to ~1500ms, p95 ~420ms. Still above target but improving. Buffer events minimal.
sam (eng-runtime): logs show remaining drops are concentrated on a handful of customer IP ranges — likely misbehaving clients not honoring backpressure.
maya (oncall): can we blacklist worst offenders temporarily? We want to prioritize graceful reconnects but block pathological clients.
kevin (network): we can add a token bucket throttle at the edge per IP/customer. I'll add rate-limit=50kb/s for flagged IPs and instrument more detailed metrics.

```
infractl: set rate-limit for ip 34.56.78.90 -> 50kb/s (flag: excessive-buffering)
```

jules (support): Customer A confirms full recovery after ~7m. Customer B still sees intermittent stalls but fewer.
maya (oncall): plan: keep reduced write buffer and fast_drop enabled across us-west for next 30m, continue sampling 10% fallback routing, blacklisting/throttling for clearly misbehaving IPs, and prepare rollback if auth QPS or reconnect errors spike.

sam (eng-runtime): long-term follow-ups: add client-side guidance on backpressure handling; add server-side circuit that proactively degrades to non-stream for inactive read windows; add per-customer streaming quotas with graceful fallback.
ravi (eng-sre): I'll create an incident postmortem stub and assign action items: throttling policy, telemetry for per-client buffer usage, and a regression test for the earlier batching tweak.

maya (oncall): thanks all. I'm closing the live page to 'monitoring' and will update in 30m. If anything regresses, re-ping with `!page oncall`.
incident-bot: NOTE: paging closed by maya (oncall). Incident severity downgraded to S3. Postmortem ticket: PM-7891.
